clue.text: Bandy Jack, for example, urged on

parts.note: in the game of bowls the jack is the small target ball, so it is an example of a bowl
to egg someone on is to urge them on

explanation.surface: Somebody spurs on a bandy-legged man named Jack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jack' looks like a name, but here it is the small white ball in lawn bowls, a game played on grass in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Bandy legs curve outward at the knee, which is exactly the shape of someone described as having that leg condition.

clue.text: Grease fit for a gusher

parts.note: grease is a lubricant, as is oil
fit means healthy, or well

explanation.surface: Some lubricant would suit an oil strike nicely.
explanation.definitionFit: A gusher is a drilled shaft from which petroleum spouts under its own pressure.

clue.text: Dancing like a doctor in fast time

indicators.note: the word in tells us the doctor piece sits within the fasting period

parts.note: Lent is the Christian season of fasting
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A doctor seems to be dancing at speed during the season of fasting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fast' suggests speed, but it is fasting: Lent.
explanation.definitionFit: Lambent describes a flame or light that flickers and plays lightly over a surface, as if moving to music.

clue.text: Only the top drawers come out of it

definitions.text: Only the top drawers come out of it

parts.words: Only the top drawers come out of it
parts.note: the drawers are those who draw pistols quickest, not chests of drawers or the social elite; only the fastest survive the shoot-out

explanation.surface: Only the best furniture, or the upper classes, emerge from some contest.
explanation.definitionFit: In a Wild West shoot-out, only the quickest pistol draw survives.

clue.text: Dirty pass

definitions.meaning: a narrow gorge or valley through which troops march in file

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means make unclean; as a noun it names a narrow mountain gorge.

clue.text: Ornamental glaze with a stripy look?

definitions.text: Ornamental glaze with a stripy look?

parts.words: Ornamental glaze with a stripy look?
parts.note: glaze here is both a pottery coating and a fixed stare; the stripy big cat gives the look its name

explanation.surface: A decorative pottery finish with banded markings.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a decorative brown banded glaze on pottery, named after the striped gem and the cat's gaze.

clue.text: One who soaks is more unreasonable

definitions.meaning: someone who steeps things, leaving them in liquid
comparative of steep, meaning excessive, as of a price

explanation.definitionFit: A person who steeps tea or laundry; and the comparative of steep in the sense of exorbitant.

clue.text: Two-master aired out for the senior officer

parts.note: a brig is a sailing ship with two masts

indicators.note: out means the letters of the word aired are put out of order

explanation.surface: A two-masted vessel is ventilated ready for a high-ranking officer.
explanation.definitionFit: A brigadier is a high army rank, above colonel, commanding a brigade.

clue.text: England's opener, winner, gets people out

indicators.note: the opener of a word is its first letter, as an opening batsman goes in first

parts.note: a victor is a winner

explanation.surface: England's opening batsman, a winner, gets the opposition out at cricket.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket picture of an opener getting batsmen out misleads; the definition describes the whole answer: one who gets people out of a property.
explanation.definitionFit: A landlord who removes tenants from a property is an evicting agent.

clue.text: Long-legged tailless bird is gaudy

indicators.note: without its tail means the last letter of the bird is dropped

parts.note: the flamingo is a long-legged pink wading bird

explanation.surface: A long-legged bird that has lost its tail looks showy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long-legged' describes the bird, helping identify it.
explanation.definitionFit: Flaming means vivid and glaring in colour, like a fierce fire.

clue.text: Unemotional type a danger to sailors

definitions.meaning: a floating mass of frozen sea water that can sink ships

explanation.definitionFit: A cold, unfeeling person is likened to a floating mass of ice, the hazard that sank the Titanic.

clue.text: Describing the first code we receive?

definitions.text: Describing the first code we receive?

parts.words: Describing the first code we receive?
parts.note: the first code each of us gets is the DNA inherited from our parents, not a law code or cipher

explanation.surface: An adjective for the first set of rules handed to us.
explanation.definitionFit: It relates to genes, the inherited code passed to us at conception.

clue.text: Belly could be a bad sign

indicators.note: could be signals that the phrase, spoken quickly, could pass for another word

parts.note: a sign is an omen, so a bad sign is a bad omen

explanation.surface: A stomach-ache might be a warning of trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: Said quickly, 'a bad omen' runs together into the word for the belly.
explanation.definitionFit: The belly is the front part of the body containing the stomach and guts.

clue.text: Framework for people in retirement

parts.note: retirement here means retiring for the night, not leaving work; the framework is one people lie on

explanation.surface: A structure supporting elderly pensioners.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the frame of a bed, used by those who retire to sleep.

clue.text: Seize eggs of one sitting

definitions.meaning: the set of eggs a hen sits on at one time

explanation.definitionFit: To grab hold of; and a batch of eggs incubated together.

clue.text: Seat of theatrical professorship

parts.note: camp means exaggerated and theatrical in manner
a chair is a professor's post at a university

explanation.surface: An academic post held by a flamboyant professor.
explanation.definitionFit: A folding stool or chair carried for use outdoors, as at a campsite.

clue.text: Cheese portion swallowed by Felix, say

indicators.note: being swallowed by something places this part inside the cat

parts.note: Felix is a famous cartoon cat, so he is an example of a cat
a member is a part or portion of a whole

explanation.surface: A piece of cheese is gobbled by a cat called Felix.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft, creamy French variety with a white rind, from Normandy.

clue.text: Degeneration of a cup following

indicators.note: following means the cup comes after the letter a

parts.note: a trophy cup is awarded as a prize

explanation.surface: A sporting cup winner's form goes downhill afterwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Atrophy is wasting away of tissue or decline through disuse.

clue.text: Part of us that gets the needle?

definitions.text: Part of us that gets the needle?

parts.words: Part of us that gets the needle?
parts.note: to get the needle means to become annoyed, but here it is a body layer pierced by a ... injection

explanation.surface: Which part of us gets irritated?
explanation.definitionFit: It is the layer of tissue beneath the skin, where an injection needle goes.

clue.text: How the bankrupt looks?

parts.note: the penniless are said to be stony broke, so the ruined person gazes in that manner, coldly and without expression

explanation.surface: A question about the expression of someone who has gone broke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stony broke' is British slang for having no money at all.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an adverb meaning coldly and without feeling, playing on the slang for penniless.

clue.text: Rhyme of feller who does the calling?

definitions.text: Rhyme of feller who does the calling?

parts.words: Rhyme of feller who does the calling?
parts.note: a word chiming with a dialect spelling of fellow, naming a person who shouts or calls out

explanation.surface: A rhyme for the chap who makes the calls.
explanation.definitionFit: One who yells is a shouter or caller, in a dialect spelling that matches feller.

clue.text: Contusions of damaged insoles

indicators.note: damaged indicates the letters of the word insoles are spoilt and rearranged

explanation.surface: Bruises caused by worn-out shoe linings.
explanation.definitionFit: Contusions are bruises, a kind of injury or wound to tissue.

clue.text: Putter-out of troublesome termite

indicators.note: troublesome suggests the letters of termite are stirred into disorder

explanation.surface: An annoying insect pest gets thrown out.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that sends out light, heat or sound, that issues or puts it out.

clue.text: Resignation of Bunthorne's bride?

definitions.meaning: the subtitle of a Gilbert and Sullivan comic opera, whose heroine milkmaid gives it its name

explanation.walkthrough: Gilbert and Sullivan wrote Victorian comic operas; this one mocks the aesthetic poet Reginald Bunthorne.
explanation.definitionFit: Forbearance under trial; and the title of the 1881 Savoy opera subtitled with the poet's bride.

clue.text: Tooth can be upset-it's the brandy!

parts.note: a cog is a tooth on a gear wheel

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means the word can is turned upside down, read backwards

explanation.surface: Someone breaks a tooth on a tin and reaches for a stiff drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Cognac is a fine French spirit distilled from wine.

clue.text: Thin paper used by lexicographer and family

parts.note: C. T. Onions was an editor of the Oxford English Dictionary
kin means family or relatives

explanation.surface: A dictionary-maker and relatives write on flimsy sheets.
explanation.definitionFit: A very thin, glossy, translucent writing paper resembling the papery layer of a bulb.

clue.text: Accessory often clasped

parts.note: the item is both fastened by a clasp and held tightly in the hand

explanation.surface: An item held tight that someone carries.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's bag carried in the hand, typically closed with a clasp.

clue.text: Glass counters?

definitions.meaning: a glass vessel with a long bent neck used in distilling
sharp replies, ripostes that counter a remark

explanation.definitionFit: Laboratory flasks for distillation; and witty rejoinders.

clue.text: Old region of low 'eights and fresh air

parts.note: heights are hills, so hilly; 'eights drops its h in the low style of speech, signalling the dropped h

indicators.note: fresh signals that the letters of air are newly arranged

explanation.surface: An ancient land of low hills and fresh breezes.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'eights shows a dropped aitch, so the hilly adjective loses its h too.
explanation.definitionFit: It was an ancient territory on the eastern Adriatic coast, in the Balkans.

clue.text: School stinks of meths, I cry out

indicators.note: crying out suggests these letters are thrown out of order

explanation.surface: A school smells of methylated spirits, and I protest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stinks' is old British schoolboy slang for the science lessons with smells and fumes.
explanation.definitionFit: The science lesson known in English boarding schools by a nickname for its smells.
